title: Seeing SDG 6 from space: local-scale monitoring of piped water and sewage system access across Africa using satellite imagery and self-supervised learning
code_availability: The code used for data preprocessing, self-supervised pretraining, held-out evaluation, and external validation is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/othmaneechc/SDG6-Tracker.
testbed_rationale: The datasets and models in this study are for socioeconomic infrastructure mapping (SDG 6 piped water and sanitation monitoring) rather than physical Earth/climate process parameterization or simulation.
pain_points: Subsurface water and sewage infrastructure are not directly visible in optical satellite imagery, forcing the model to rely on indirect built-environment and settlement proxies.
Cloud cover limits optical imagery availability and quality in certain regions.
Decoupling between settlement morphology and actual service delivery can lead to errors.
Indicator definition mismatch between survey labels (sewer connection access) and international validation targets (WHO/UNICEF safely managed sanitation, which encompasses septic tanks and latrines).
Spatial data leakage risk requiring survey-location-level rather than interview-level data splits.
extraction_notes: The arXiv identifier header states version v6 dated 30 May 2026. Pretrained models and inference results are shared on Zenodo.
